recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed in core unless the work group intentionally reopens the broader HumanName example semantics and decides to replace the current NameUse nickname example with a different NameUse.
issue_request: FHIR-16963 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes change request from the STU3 ballot asking to correct HumanName narrative examples and guidance: replace invalid Use = common in the Jock nickname row, change the HumanName text/parts update rule from an address to a name, and broaden affiliate-specific search guidance to include implementation guide authors and specific cultures or environments.
initial_application: The Jira comment records application as svn 14288. In git, 3fd0ecd870122c5cc18974817f0837553468ad28 is explicitly tied to GF#16963/FHIR-16963 and changed source/datatypes.html so the HumanName update rule says a name and the search-guidance sentence includes HL7 affiliates and others producing implementation guides. That issue-tagged commit did not change the nickname-row wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists HumanName in [types] and maps data types to the datatypes page, so source/datatypes.html is in current build scope for the HumanName narrative. Current source/datatypes.html says the Jock nickname row has Use = nickname, and source/datatypes/humanname.xml defines nickname as a name used to address the person informally. Later commit 5cbc14c7d0f361941099bf72066b75c3f74f6d4f changed the example from Use = common to Use = nickname as part of R5 MnM changes, so changing it now to the Jira proposal's Use = usual would undo later source evolution and make the nickname example less precise.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because the current source already contains the substantive HumanName corrections and no longer contains the invalid Use = common wording in the HumanName nickname example.
